specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** bloom-level-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of twelve learning objectives under the Bloom cognitive level its verb signals, with at least 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Bloom's Taxonomy, Bloom Cognitive Levels, Learning Objective, Measurable Verb (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each objective the learner commits one of six levels. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct level column in Content. Mastery is at least 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt. Reading the level table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The level depends on the topic. (2) "Identify" and "explain" are the same level. (3) A harder-sounding verb is always a higher level. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying objectives by level is an Understand-level action that builds the skill reviewers need when they compare an outcome with its activities. Two objectives per level, each with an unambiguous verb, teach the learner to read the verb first. **Content:** The six levels: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, Create. The twelve objectives: | # | Objective shown to the learner | Correct level | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | List the five parts of a lesson plan. | Remember | "List" asks for recall. | | 2 | Name the three main types of rock. | Remember | "Name" asks for recall. | | 3 | Explain in your own words why the seasons change. | Understand | "Explain" asks for meaning in your own words. | | 4 | Summarize the main idea of a news article. | Understand | "Summarize" asks for a restatement of meaning. | | 5 | Calculate the perimeter of a garden from its side lengths. | Apply | "Calculate" uses a procedure on a new case. | | 6 | Use a map scale to find the distance between two towns. | Apply | "Use" applies a rule in a new situation. | | 7 | Distinguish a fact from an opinion in a short article. | Analyze | "Distinguish" separates parts and sees how they differ. | | 8 | Differentiate a cause from an effect in a historical event. | Analyze | "Differentiate" separates parts and relates them. | | 9 | Judge which of two experiment designs is fairer, and justify the choice. | Evaluate | "Judge" and "justify" use criteria to decide. | | 10 | Critique a persuasive essay using a checklist of criteria. | Evaluate | "Critique" judges against criteria. | | 11 | Design an experiment to test how light affects plant growth. | Create | "Design" produces something new. | | 12 | Compose a short story that uses three given vocabulary words. | Create | "Compose" produces something new. | **Provenance:** The objectives are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The levels and their verbs follow the chapter section "Bloom Cognitive Levels", which follows the 2001 revision of the taxonomy. **Rules:** Each objective has exactly one correct level, two per level. The level is determined by the main verb. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one objective and the six levels. 2. The learner may open the level table. Opening it does not change the score. 3. The learner chooses a level, and the choice is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After objective 12 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 12 objectives in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [level]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [level]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 12 correct on the first attempt". At 10 or more it adds "You can read the level in a verb." Below 10 it lists the Why text of each missed objective. **Starting State:** The first objective, the six levels, and the level table closed. The question shown is "Which Bloom level does this objective ask for?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists six levels in the order remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, and create, and says this book uses the 2001 revision.
